segments.he: עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה וְתַחֲנוּנִים מוֹצֵא אֲבֵדוֹתָיו
segments.en: In this matter many people err greatly, each one saying: "If I had a livelihood I would serve Hashem." But if so, by their own reasoning, the Holy One blessed be He is coming to him, Heaven forbid, with grievance and false accusation — He wants him to serve Hashem and study Torah even though he cannot, because of the pressure of livelihood. If so, he is questioning Hashem's judgments, as if Hashem, Heaven forbid, were distorting justice against him. And this flaw is very great, for when one questions Hashem's judgments this is the very essence of the flaw of judgment, from which all the corruptions described above arise. Therefore everyone who genuinely cares for his own welfare must be very careful not to speak such words, but must know and believe that his free choice depends precisely upon the situation in which Hashem conducts Himself with him — and must believe that everything is for his own good, and be accustomed to say: "All that the Merciful One does, He does for good," and certainly there is a way through precisely this pressure and suffering and confusion that one can draw close to Hashem.

segments.he: הַכְּלָל שֶׁהָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל כָּל יָמָיו לְבַקֵּשׁ וּלְחַפֵּשׂ מְאד מְאד אַחַר אֲבֵדוֹתָיו. כִּי זֶה עִקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה וְכַנַּ"ל. וְאִם יְבַקֵּשׁ וִיחַפֵּשׂ הֵיטֵב בְּוַדַּאי יִמְצָא כַּנַּ"ל וַאֲפִלּוּ בְּעֵת שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לִמְצא עֲדַיִן, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן עַל יְדֵי כָּל יְגִיעָה וְחִפּוּשׂ כְּבָר מָצָא הַרְבֵּה. כִּי אֵין שׁוּם יְגִיעָה וּבַקָּשָׁה נֶאֱבָד כְּלָל וּבְוַדַּאי מָצָא מַה שֶּׁמָּצָא עַל יְדֵי כָּל דִּבּוּר וְדִבּוּר וְעַל יְדֵי כָּל יְגִיעָה וְחִפּוּשׂ כִּי לֵית רְעוּתָא טָבָא דְּאִתְאַבֵּד.
segments.en: And if it is hard for him to accept and bear the suffering and the pressure, let him cry out and pray to Hashem to save him and help him — and through this very act he draws close to Hashem and serves Him. For Hashem desires the prayers of Yisrael, as it is written: "Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you and you shall honor Me" [Tehillim 50:15]. For there is no counsel and no stratagem against all the troubles and trials and pressures and burdens of livelihood that pass over every person at every time — except to cry out and cry and beseech and implore before Hashem, and to weep before Him like an infant weeping before its father to have its needs fulfilled. And when one goes in this path, one will always gain greatly — a true and eternal gain. For most often his petition will be effective, since Hashem hears the prayer of every mouth. And even if sometimes, Heaven forbid, his prayer is not accepted — sometimes He listens and sometimes He does not — even so he has gained by having drawn himself closer to Hashem through this. For nothing draws and attaches a person to Hashem like prayer, which is the very essence of Israel's bond and deveykus with Hashem.

segments.he: וְכָל אֶחָד כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ חֵלֶק יוֹתֵר בְּהַבַּקָּשָׁה וְהַחִפּוּשׂ אַשְׁרֵי לוֹ וּלְפוּם צַעֲרָא אַגְרָא. שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהִתְיַגַּע וְהִצְטַעֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ יוֹתֵר עַל הָאֲבֵדוֹת וְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לְבַקְּשָׁם וּלְחַפְּשָׂם בִּתְפִלָּה וְתַחֲנוּנִים וּבְגַעְגּוּעִים וְהִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּת וְהִתְקָרְבוּת לְצַדִּיקִים וּכְשֵׁרִים אֲמִתִּיִּים וְסָבַל בִּזְיוֹנוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים הַרְבֵּה עַל יְדֵי זֶה. וּכְמוֹ כֵן יִזְכֶּה בְּיוֹתֵר שֶׁיַּחֲזִירוּ לוֹ אֲבֵדוֹתָיו בְּשָׁלוֹם.
segments.en: But one who says "if things were such-and-such I would study Torah etc." — this is no counsel at all and he causes himself a great flaw, the flaw of judgment, as described above. For everyone must seek Hashem from wherever he is, as it is written: "From there you shall seek Hashem your G-d and you shall find Him" [Devarim 4:29] — from there specifically, from the place where you are, from whatever passes over you, as conveyed in the name of the Baal Shem Tov of blessed memory.

segments.he: וְהַכּל בְּכחַ הַצַּדִּיק הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁמְּחַפֵּשׂ תָּמִיד אַחַר כָּל הָאֲבֵדוֹת וּמְחַזֵּק לֵב כָּל אֶחָד לְבַל יִתְיָאֲשׁוּ עַצְמָן בְּשׁוּם אפֶן מִלְּבַקֵּשׁ וּלְחַפֵּשׂ אַחַר הָאֲבֵדוֹת בִּתְפִלָּה וּבְתַחֲנוּנִים וְכוּ'. וּלְהִתְגַּעְגֵּעַ מְאד אַחֲרֵיהֶם וּלְצַפּוֹת לִישׁוּעָה תָּמִיד שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִזְכּוּ שֶׁעַל יָדָם יִמָּצְאוּ כָּל הָאֲבֵדוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם בִּמְהֵרָה בְּיָמֵינוּ אָמֵן:
segments.en: When a person has distanced himself from Hashem, Heaven forbid — and all the more so when he falls into evil desires and transgressions, Heaven forbid — he is in the aspect of "Rachel weeping for her children" [Yirmeyahu 31:15]. For the Shechinah, which is the holiness of Yisrael, is called Rachel, as is known. And then she is in the aspect of "like a ewe before its shearers she was silent" — that is, the holiness of the soul of Yisrael is among the kelipas and the other sides that press and constrict her. And from the great weakness she experiences due to the abundance of his sins, she is like a ewe before its shearers — they shear and rob her and take away her splendor and her glory, and she is silenced among them. And then she is in the aspect of "the Shechinah says: I am burdened by my head, I am burdened by my arm" as our Rabbis of blessed memory taught.

segments.he: (הִלְכוֹת בִּרְכַּת הַפֵֶּרוֹת הֲלָכָה ה אוֹת א גד):
segments.en: But when this very distant person is aroused within his very distance and does not despair himself in any way, and weeps and cries out to Hashem always — this is the aspect of "A voice is heard in Ramah — lamentation, bitter weeping — Rachel weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted for her children, for they are gone" [Yirmeyahu 31:15]. That is: the holiness of the soul of Yisrael, which is the aspect of Rachel, is weeping bitterly for her children — which are the good deeds she has lost through her evil desires, for good deeds are called "children," as our Rabbis say that the primary offspring of the righteous are good deeds. And she weeps with great bitterness — in the aspect of lamentation, bitter weeping — until the voice is heard in Ramah, meaning her voice is heard in the heights of Heaven.
